items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I had to compose a piece that contains the Marseilliers and the Stars Spangled Banner.

ctx.x: It doesn't look like it's hurt you anymore.

I'd rather be a side man. Sure. And then you don't have to put up with the captain. And then there's women. And then when I do, I get brainstormed. I had a doctor, he says a letter to my sweetheart. I said that sounds nice. And you know what it was? His whole life. I had to put music to when he was in the army and when he got out of the army, when he recorded his wife, when the first baby was born, all that. He said, you need a score for that. You need an arranger to sit down and time all that stuff. You know?…
This was during what? How did this work? The Louisiana Purchase.
